text:
maria: Kicking off a quick thread — ran the A/B on Transformer Engine toggles for FP8 on H100 and L40S. posting raw notes and a small repro.
sam: nice, short summary first? any regressions or just noise?
jordan: TL;DR: H100 FP8 kernel-A on TE v0.9 gives +18% tokens/s vs INT8 for batch=8 but L40S shows instability in kv-cache warmup (spikes + tail latency). more below.
lee: what configs did you flip in TE? kernel selection + autotune?
maria: toggles: \n- TE_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=kernel-A,kernel-B,kernel-fallback\n- ENABLE_FP8_QUANT=1\n- AUTOTUNE_BATCH=off (to isolate kernel perf)\n- KV_PREFETCH_THRESH=0.3
sam: ok. any changes to patch layout or GEMM tiling?
jordan: none. we only changed TransformerEngine path selection order and quant params.
maria: repro snippet I used on staging (simplified):
```bash
export TE_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=kernel-A,kernel-B
export ENABLE_FP8_QUANT=1
python perf_client.py --model redwood/gpt-medium --batch 8 --seq 512 --requests 200
```
perf-bot: perf run complete: p50=54ms, p95=132ms, tokens/s=12500 (H100, kernel-A)
anya: can you paste L40S numbers side-by-side?
maria: L40S (same config): p50=68ms, p95=220ms, tokens/s=9800, plus ~1.8% request failures (KV miss causing fallback). logs show kv_cache_replay errors at the same sequence offsets.
sam: failure rate small but p95 doubling is concerning. is this correlated with sequence length distribution?
jordan: yes — when input has long prefixes (>=1k tokens), KV cache write bursts collide with our async prefetch queue on L40S. kernel-A has tighter shared-memory usage which increases eviction rate.
lee: sounds like memory pressure -> eviction -> cache miss -> fallback path -> regen -> latency spike. can we tweak KV_PREFETCH_THRESH or async queue depth?
maria: tried KV_PREFETCH_THRESH=0.5: p95 improved to 160ms but tokens/s down 6%. so it's a tradeoff.
sam: what about switching kernel order for L40S automatically? route to kernel-B when sequence>512 or when warmup pattern detected?
jordan: implemented a lightweight heuristic: if avg_seq_len>512 OR kv_eviction_rate>0.5% then prefer kernel-B. A/B results: L40S p95=110ms, tokens/s=10300, failures -> 0.2%.
anya: nice. any quality delta from calibration differences between kernels?
maria: ran eval subset (1000 prompts) comparing FP8 kernel-A vs kernel-B on H100: chrF & perplexity delta within noise (<0.3%); no significant hallucination patterns.
sam: what about long-term stability? flakiness in nightly runs?
jordan: observed occasional TE assertion in kernel-A on L40S under heavy multi-tenant loads — root cause: a race in shared scratch allocator. created PR#4527 with fix and added a stress test that simulates concurrent kv writes.
lee: good. CI/infra side: we should gate kernel-A rollout on that PR and enable a rollout policy with gradual traffic and rapid fallback to INT8.
maria: agree. planned rollout: \n- Canary: 5% traffic on H100 only (kernel-A allowed)\n- Canary: 1% on L40S with kernel-A disabled until PR merged\n- Autoswitch: enable heuristic that routes L40S traffic to kernel-B for seq>512
perf-bot: canary metrics template: include p50/p95, tokens/s, kv_eviction_rate, te_asserts, fallback_count.
sam: also add memory_headroom metric and async_prefetch_queue_len to dashboard.
jordan: small note: enabling AUTOTUNE_BATCH back made kernel-A throughput better on H100 (another +6%) but reintroduced jitter on L40S during warmup. i'd keep AUTOTUNE_BATCH off for now until KV allocator fix lands.
maria: action items: \n1) jordan -> PR#4527 (allocator fix) + stress test (done, but want 2 reviewers)\n2) eng-infra (lee) -> create canary pipeline with metrics and auto-fallback rule\n3) perf (sam) -> run overnight mixed seq-length workload with kernel-A on H100 and kernel-B fallback on L40S\n4) anya -> notify product about potential small perf delta during next release note
lee: I'll spin up the canary job and add alerts for te_assert and kv_eviction_rate > 0.5%.
anya: thanks, will draft a short note.
maria: attaching a couple logs for anyone who wants the raw traces (excerpt):
```json
{
  "ts": 1852300000,
  "event": "kv_eviction",
  "model": "gpt-medium",
  "seq": 1536,
  "alloc_free_mb": 120
}
{
  "ts": 1852300065,
  "event": "te_assert",
  "kernel": "kernel-A",
  "msg": "scratch allocator double-free"
}
```
sam: thanks. i'm comfortable with canary plan once PR has 2 reviews + stress green.
jordan: i'll ping reviewers. also adding a small metric to measure "kernel_switch_count" per request so we can quantify fallback churn.
maria: perfect. aiming to start canary tomorrow morning. any objections?
anya: none from product.
lee: no objections.
maria: cool — closing thread. will post follow-ups in eng-runtime once canary live.
perf-bot: thread archived (auto)
